results.title: Supersoluble groups via cyclic normal series
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is supersoluble if there are a natural number $k$ and subgroups $1 = S_0 \le S_1 \le \cdots \le S_k = G$, each normal in $G$, such that for every $i < k$ we have $S_i \le S_{i+1}$ and there is an element $x \in S_{i+1}$ such that $S_{i+1}$ is generated by $x$ and $S_i$; that is, every factor $S_{i+1}/S_i$ is cyclic.

results.title: Abnormal subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is abnormal in $G$ if every element $g \in G$ lies in the subgroup generated by $H$ and its conjugate $gHg^{-1}$.

results.title: Abnormal supersoluble trifactorizations (Kourovka 19.100)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that for every finite group $G$ and all subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of $G$ that are abnormal in $G$ and supersoluble, if $G = AB = BC = CA$ as sets, then $G$ is supersoluble.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 19.100 has a positive answer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $A$, $B$, $C$ be subgroups of $G$, each abnormal in $G$ and supersoluble, such that $G = AB = BC = CA$ as sets. Then $G$ is supersoluble.

results.title: Supersoluble group (generator form)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is supersoluble when there are a natural number $n$ and elements $g_0, \dots, g_{n-1}$ of $G$ that generate $G$ such that, for every $i \le n$, the subgroup $G_i = \langle g_j : j < i \rangle$ is normal in $G$.

results.title: Monakhov's condition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ satisfies Monakhov's condition when every maximal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of prime factors of the order of $X$ if $X$ is finite, and is empty if $X$ is infinite.

results.title: Chief factor of rank above a bound
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ has a chief factor of rank greater than a natural number $r$ when there are a chief factor $A / B$ of $G$, a prime $p$ and a natural number $k > r$ such that the index $[A : B]$ equals $p^k$.

results.title: Groups of p-length at most one
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $p$, a group $G$ has $p$-length at most $1$ when there are normal subgroups $N \le M$ of $G$ such that $N$ is finite of order not divisible by $p$, the index $[M : N]$ equals $p^k$ for some natural number $k$ (an infinite index counting as $0$), and the index $[G : M]$ is finite and not divisible by $p$.

results.title: Kourovka 19.55(a) (Monakhov): every non-abelian simple group occurs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that for every finite non-abelian simple group $S$ there is a finite group $G$ such that $S$ is a composition factor of $G$ and every maximal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of primes dividing the order of $X$.

results.title: Kourovka 19.55(b) (Monakhov): unbounded Fitting height
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that for every natural number $h$ there is a finite soluble group $G$ whose Fitting height is greater than $h$ and in which every maximal subgroup $M$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of primes dividing the order of $X$.

results.title: Unbounded chief-factor rank under Monakhov's condition (the claim)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every natural number $r$ there is a finite soluble group $G$ satisfying Monakhov's condition (every maximal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of prime divisors of $|X|$) that has a chief factor $A/B$ of order $p^k$ for some prime $p$ and some $k > r$. This is the answer to Kourovka 19.55(b) for the rank.

results.title: Kourovka 19.55(b) (Monakhov): p-length at most one
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that for every finite soluble group $G$ in which every maximal subgroup $H$ with $\pi(H) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of primes dividing the order of $X$, and for every prime $p$, the group $G$ has $p$-length at most $1$: there are normal subgroups $N \le M$ of $G$ such that $p$ does not divide $|N|$, the index $[M : N]$ is a power of $p$, and $p$ does not divide $[G : M]$.

results.title: Moretó: every non-abelian simple group occurs in Kourovka 19.55(a)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite non-abelian simple group $S$ there is a finite group $G$ such that $S$ is a composition factor of $G$ and every maximal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of primes dividing the order of $X$.

results.title: Moretó: soluble groups in Kourovka 19.55 have unbounded Fitting height
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $h$ there is a finite soluble group $G$ whose Fitting height is greater than $h$ and in which every maximal subgroup $M$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of primes dividing the order of $X$.

results.title: Unbounded chief-factor rank under Monakhov's condition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $r$ there is a finite soluble group $G$ such that every maximal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of prime divisors of $|X|$, and $G$ has a chief factor $A/B$ (normal subgroups $B < A$ of $G$ with no normal subgroup of $G$ strictly between them) of order $p^k$ for some prime $p$ and some $k > r$.

results.title: Moretó: soluble groups in Kourovka 19.55 have p-length at most one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite soluble group in which every maximal subgroup $H$ with $\pi(H) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of primes dividing the order of $X$. Then for every prime $p$ the group $G$ has $p$-length at most $1$: there are normal subgroups $N \le M$ of $G$ such that $p$ does not divide $|N|$, the index $[M : N]$ is a power of $p$, and $p$ does not divide $[G : M]$.

results.title: Polar decomposition of a complex square matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a square complex matrix indexed by a finite type, and let $A^*$ be its conjugate transpose. Then there are a unitary matrix $U$ and a positive semidefinite matrix $P$ such that $P^2 = A^* A$ and $A = UP$.

results.title: Uniqueness of the polar decomposition of an invertible matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $A$ be a square matrix over $\mathbb{K}$, indexed by a finite type, with $\det A \neq 0$. Then there are a unitary matrix $U$ and a positive-definite matrix $P$ with $A = UP$, and they are unique: if $U'$ is unitary, $P'$ is positive definite and $A = U'P'$, then $U' = U$ and $P' = P$.

results.title: Polar decomposition of invertible real matrices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a real square matrix with rows and columns indexed by a finite set, and suppose $\det A \ne 0$. Then there are an orthogonal matrix $O$ and a positive-definite symmetric matrix $S$ with $A = OS$, and they are unique: if $O'$ is orthogonal, $S'$ is positive-definite symmetric and $A = O'S'$, then $O' = O$ and $S' = S$.

results.title: Polar decomposition of invertible complex matrices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a complex square matrix with rows and columns indexed by a finite set, and suppose $\det A \ne 0$. Then there are a unitary matrix $U$ and a positive-definite Hermitian matrix $P$ with $A = UP$, and they are unique: if $U'$ is unitary, $P'$ is positive-definite Hermitian and $A = U'P'$, then $U' = U$ and $P' = P$.

results.title: Multiplicative order modulo $n$

results.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $a$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $a$ coprime to $p$. Writing $\operatorname{ord}_n(b)$ for the multiplicative order of $b$ modulo $n$, the order $\operatorname{ord}_{p^2}(a + kp)$ is either $\operatorname{ord}_p(a)$ or $p \cdot \operatorname{ord}_p(a)$.

results.title: Gauss's theorem on primitive roots modulo prime powers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $g$ be a natural number that is a primitive root modulo $p$, where a primitive root modulo $n$ is a residue class modulo $n$ of multiplicative order $\varphi(n)$. Then there is a natural number $k$ such that $g + kp$ is a primitive root modulo $p^\ell$ for every $\ell \ge 2$.

results.title: Exactly one lift of a primitive root fails modulo $p^2$

results.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $g$ be a natural number that is a primitive root modulo $p$, where a primitive root modulo $n$ is a residue class modulo $n$ of multiplicative order $\varphi(n)$. Then there is exactly one $m \in \{0, 1, \dots, p - 1\}$ such that $g + mp$ is not a primitive root modulo $p^2$, and $g + kp$ is a primitive root modulo $p^2$ for every other $k \in \{0, 1, \dots, p - 1\}$.

results.title: Power maps on the fibers modulo $p^2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $a$ be a unit modulo $p^2$, and let $n$ be a natural number coprime to $p$ and to the multiplicative order of $a$. Writing $P_b$ for the set of units $x$ modulo $p^2$ with $x \equiv b \pmod p$, the map $x \mapsto x^n$ is injective on $P_a$, maps $P_a$ onto $P_{a^n}$, and preserves the multiplicative order of every element of $P_a$.

results.title: Octanacci window
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The octanacci window is the sequence $(w_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of $8$-tuples of natural numbers with $w_0 = (1, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64)$ and, if $w_n = (a_1, \dots, a_8)$, then $w_{n+1} = (a_2, \dots, a_8, a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_8)$. The octanacci numbers $f_n$ are the first entries of these tuples, so $w_n = (f_n, f_{n+1}, \dots, f_{n+7})$.

results.title: Octanacci numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The octanacci sequence $(f_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of natural numbers is defined by $f_0 = f_1 = 1$, $f_n = 2^{n-1}$ for $2 \le n \le 7$, and $f_n = f_{n-1} + f_{n-2} + \dots + f_{n-8}$ for $n \ge 8$. It begins $1, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 255, \dots$, and its generating function is $1/(1 - t - t^2 - \dots - t^8)$.

results.title: N-step Fibonacci numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $N$, the $N$-step Fibonacci numbers $F^{(N)}_n$ ($n \ge 0$), in the convention of Noe and Post, are defined by $F^{(N)}_0 = 0$, $F^{(N)}_1 = 1$ and, for $n \ge 2$, $F^{(N)}_n = \sum_{i=1}^{N} F^{(N)}_{n-i}$, where a term whose index $n - i$ is negative counts as $0$. In particular $F^{(0)}_n = 0$ for $n \ge 2$.

results.title: Recurrence for the N-step Fibonacci numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $N$ and $n$, the $N$-step Fibonacci numbers $F^{(N)}$ satisfy $F^{(N)}_{n+2} = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} F^{(N)}_{\max(n+1-i,\,0)}$.

results.title: The frame operator is bounded below

results.title: Inverse frame operator

results.title: Peak of a permutation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$. A position $i$ is a peak of $\sigma$ if $i + 2 < n$ and $\sigma(i) < \sigma(i+1) > \sigma(i+2)$. Thus the peak entry is $\sigma(i+1)$, and the position recorded is $i$, that of the first of the three entries.

results.title: Valley of a permutation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$. A position $i$ is a valley of $\sigma$ if $i + 2 < n$ and $\sigma(i) > \sigma(i+1) < \sigma(i+2)$. Thus the valley entry is $\sigma(i+1)$, and the position recorded is $i$, that of the first of the three entries.

results.title: Number of double ascents
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, $\mathrm{dasc}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ that are double ascents of $\sigma$.

results.title: Number of double descents
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, $\mathrm{ddes}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ that are double descents of $\sigma$.

results.title: Number of peaks of a permutation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ written in one-line notation, $\operatorname{pk}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ with $i + 2 < n$ and $\sigma(i) < \sigma(i + 1) > \sigma(i + 2)$, that is, the number of peaks of $\sigma$.

results.title: Number of valleys of a permutation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ written in one-line notation, $\operatorname{vl}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ with $i + 2 < n$ and $\sigma(i) > \sigma(i + 1) < \sigma(i + 2)$, that is, the number of valleys of $\sigma$.

results.title: Number of positions with two successors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, exactly $n - 2$ of the positions $i \in \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ satisfy $i + 2 < n$, where $n - 2$ is truncated subtraction (it is $0$ when $n < 2$).

results.title: Local shape of a position in a permutation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $i$ be a position. If $i + 2 < n$, then $i$ is exactly one of a double ascent, a double descent, a peak or a valley of $\sigma$; otherwise $i$ is none of them. That is, the number of these four properties that $i$ has is $1$ when $i + 2 < n$ and $0$ otherwise.

results.title: Sum of the four local statistics of a permutation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, and write $\mathrm{dasc}(\sigma)$, $\mathrm{ddes}(\sigma)$, $\mathrm{pk}(\sigma)$ and $\mathrm{vl}(\sigma)$ for its numbers of double ascents, double descents, peaks and valleys. Then $\mathrm{dasc}(\sigma) + \mathrm{ddes}(\sigma) + \mathrm{pk}(\sigma) + \mathrm{vl}(\sigma) = n - 2$, where $n - 2$ is truncated subtraction (it is $0$ when $n < 2$).

results.title: EDGE DOMINATING SET instances
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of EDGE DOMINATING SET is a triple $(n, E, K)$ of a natural number $n$ (the vertex count), a finite list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers (the edge list) and a natural number $K$ (the bound).

results.title: Edge-list adjacency for EDGE DOMINATING SET
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers and natural numbers $u$ and $v$, the Boolean adjacency of $u$ and $v$ in $E$ is true exactly when $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ occurs in $E$.

results.title: Well-formed EDGE DOMINATING SET instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance with vertex count $n$, edge list $E$ and bound $K$ is well formed when $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(a, b)$ in $E$ satisfies $a < n$, $b < n$ and $a \ne b$, and $(b, a)$ does not occur in $E$. Thus $E$ lists the edges of a simple graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n - 1$, each once and in one orientation.

results.title: Feasible EDGE DOMINATING SET instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance with vertex count $n$, edge list $E$ and bound $K$ is feasible when some sublist $D$ of $E$ (its entries taken in order) has at most $K$ entries and dominates every edge of $E$: for every $e \in E$ there is $d \in D$ such that one of the two entries of $d$ equals one of the two entries of $e$.

results.title: The EDGE DOMINATING SET decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: EDGE DOMINATING SET is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to an EDGE DOMINATING SET instance $(n, E, K)$ that is well formed and feasible, that is, some sublist of $E$ with at most $K$ entries contains, for every edge of $E$, an edge sharing an endpoint with it. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.

results.title: EDGE DOMINATING SET is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The EDGE DOMINATING SET decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
